title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence: U.S. and International Approaches and Considerations for Congress (CRS R48555)
notes: Primary nonpartisan CRS report (Version 4, June 4, 2025). Cited for the US-vs-international AI regulation comparison under Social.
claims: No broad federal AI regulatory authority enacted; US approach cautious on private-sector AI, focused on federal-use oversight
States enacting their own AI laws in the absence of federal regulation (patchwork concern)
EU: broad risk-based approach (EU AI Act); China: vertical, technology-specific framework; UK: measured approach
Shift from Biden-era AI safety focus toward security concerns in the second Trump Administration
Policy options for Congress: leverage existing frameworks, create new authorities, support US AI development, engage internationally
